provider: Lemmy + pict-rs — per-instance image store, no per-user quota

free_tier.stated: No per-user quota in Lemmy's own schema — the bound is pict-rs (the separate Rust image server) and the instance's disk. Upload is gated per-instance by the `image_upload` / `image_mode` local-site flag rather than by bytes.

per_object_cap.stated: per-object-cap set by pict-rs (`max_file_size`, commonly 40 MB

tooling: Lemmy API v3: POST /api/v3/pictrs/image (multipart) or /api/v3/upload; needs a JWT from POST /api/v3/user/login. pict-rs itself exposes POST /image on its own port (often 8080) — on instances that expose it, that is a cleaner upload path than the Lemmy API.
chaining: Lemmy is the weakest of the family: most large instances now REQUIRE an application (lemmy.world registration_mode = 'RequireApplication'), and `image_mode` is frequently set to block uploads entirely or to proxy-only. Multiplier depends entirely on finding a permissive instance.
